mechanism_claims.claim_text: AR-23 directly damaged enveloped virions: TEM showed HSV-1 particles losing the envelope and SARS-CoV-2 particles losing/detaching spike-associated envelope features after 25 µM AR-23 treatment.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: AR-23 against enveloped viruses HSV-1 and SARS-CoV-2
direct_assay_types: transmission electron microscopy of purified virions after AR-23 exposure
mechanism_claims.limitations: TEM supports envelope disruption for HSV-1 and SARS-CoV-2, not a quantified universal mechanism for every virus tested.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Plaque assays place the antiviral effect in extracellular/early infection stages: co-treatment and virus pre-treatment were active for enveloped viruses, while cell pre-treatment and post-treatment were inactive or only slight.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: AR-23 against HSV-1, MeV, HPIV-2, HCoV-229E, SARS-CoV-2, and PV-1 comparison
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is mechanism localization by treatment timing and virus envelope dependence, not a molecular binding target assignment.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: RT-qPCR after virus pre-treatment showed dose-dependent reduction of HSV-1 UL54/UL52/UL27 and HCoV-229E/SARS-CoV-2 N/S gene expression, supporting reduced infection rather than defining a direct intracellular target.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: AR-23 virus pre-treatment assay molecular readout

mechanism_claims.limitations: The qPCR readout follows virus pre-treatment and is not promoted to direct inhibition of transcription or translation machinery.
